canonical_statement: Let X be a regular topological space, let (mu_epsilon) be probability measures satisfying a large-deviation principle with good rate function I at speed a_epsilon tending to zero, and let F : X -> R be bounded and continuous. Then lim as epsilon tends to zero of a_epsilon * log(integral exp(F/a_epsilon) d mu_epsilon) equals sup over x of (F(x) - I(x)).
domain_and_universes: A topological measurable space X; probability measures mu_epsilon; positive real speed a_epsilon -> 0; good rate I : X -> ENNReal (or an audited equivalent); bounded continuous F : X -> R
quantifiers: X and its compatible topological/measurable structure
mu_epsilon : Measure X, each a probability measure
a_epsilon : R, positive and tending to zero
I : X -> [0,infinity], a good rate function
F : X -> R, bounded and continuous
hypotheses: mu_epsilon satisfies the full large-deviation principle at speed a_epsilon with rate I
I is good (lower semicontinuous with compact sublevel sets)
the exponential integral is interpreted in a type supporting its extended-real boundary cases
conclusion: Laplace asymptotic: a_epsilon * log Integral exp(F/a_epsilon) d mu_epsilon converges to sup_x (F x - I x)

alternate_encodings.target: inverse-speed convention: (1/beta) * log Integral exp(beta*F), beta -> infinity
unbounded continuous F with a tail or moment condition
alternate_encodings.relationship: strict generalization, not interchangeable with the frozen root
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: excluded from root; may be a later variant

excluded_degenerate_cases: Zero or negative speeds, a merely weak LDP without exponential tightness, and unbounded F without a tail condition are outside the frozen root. Empty-space and infinite-value conventions require explicit statement-phase probes.
